raw.excerpt: OverviewJoin a team where innovation meets mission.
raw.description:
Overview

Join a team where innovation meets mission. Our AI, cloud, cyber, and modernization solutions save agencies thousands of hours, safeguard national security, and strengthen health and humanitarian missions worldwide. With 1,700+ team members, 1,500+ AI/data experts, and 100+ prime contracts, we deliver at scale and with purpose.

We’ve been recognized as a Top Workplace by the Washington Post for six straight years and named to the Inc. 5000 Fastest Growing Private Companies 13 of the past 14 years. Credence is a welcoming home for those looking to grow and contribute to positive change. We encourage all employees to expand beyond their boundaries, dive into important world-changing Federal challenges.

Position Summary

The Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract (HASC) brings together exceptional institutional support experience, technical leadership, and an unmatched commitment to US missions. HASC supports the U.S. Department of State’s (DOS) humanitarian assistance, disaster response, and foreign assistance across multiple bureaus. Team Credence, through the HASC, delivers operational and administrative support to provide and coordinate humanitarian assistance and maintain 24/7 response capability.

Credence has an immediate need for the Humanitarian Health Advisor, Ebola Response Consultant who will serve as part of the Disaster Humanitarian and Response (DHR) Bureau’s Technical Quality and Assurance (TQA) Office, within the Health Unit. They will be responsible for working on DHR’s response to the current Ebola disease outbreak in West/Central Africa.

The Consultant will also work with other sectors of the office including protection; water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH); nutrition; natural hazards and shelter and settlements, to provide a multidisciplinary approach to providing life-saving program to disaster affected populations. S/he will support DHR’s approach to emergency health activities within the team and assist in developing response strategies and provide technical support to humanitarian health programming in the Department of State. The Advisor will receive day-to-day guidance from the Senior Health Advisor. S/he will work in close coordination with other Health Advisors.

Scope:

The Consultant will provide technical advisory services to the TQA Office in support of the Department of State’s humanitarian health programming. In addition, the consultant will support DHR’s coordination with the Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy and other bureaus at State and the interagency, including HHS/ASPR, OGA, and CDC.

Overall, the Consultant is expected to show strong independent initiative and work with minimal supervision and engage with stakeholders in close collaboration with and under the direction of the Senior Health Advisor and Ebola Response Leads. Day-to-day oversight of the position will be provided by the Senior Health Advisor, with formal supervisory and evaluation functions performed by a Credence contract supervisor.

The main roles and responsibilities of the Consultant will be:

  • Advise the Response Lead on appropriate strategies on humanitarian response modalities that best enable Ebola outbreak response activities considering lessons learned from past Ebola outbreaks. Identify critical gaps that facilitate the pillars of response and advise the DHR leadership on these strategies.
  • Liaise directly with technical lead and pillar leads of the response at post, and in DC.
  • Advise the DHR Programs Lead on programming. And advise on when other technical sectors need to provide analysis and technical assistance for the response.
  • Engage with the national health cluster and sub-clusters to understand humanitarian gaps, challenges and response plans; attend regular cluster meetings.
  • Evaluate and document health programming gaps and assess the performance of current DHR awards in responding to these gaps.
  • Coordinate with humanitarian partners to understand humanitarian gaps and challenges in light of the Ebola response and understand the integration of health humanitarian actions and Ebola response actions.
  • Attend pillar meetings to understand technical gaps and how they are exacerbated by humanitarian needs or could be better supported through humanitarian enablers.
  • Serve as a USG humanitarian health sector resource person, assist in strategy development and provide expert technical and organizational leadership in sectoral activity as part of Ebola Response.
  • Advise and support technical and strategic thinking for health activities, interventions, and recommendation discussions. Develop sector strategies, guidance, and recommendations (in coordination with other sectors when required) for disaster and humanitarian response; and provide technical support for DHR staff at Post, and other offices within State.
  • Advise and support discussions on emergency health activities with NGO partners and other Department of State staff working in humanitarian health.
  • Provide technical review of proposals submitted by NGO and UN partners for humanitarian health programs. Apply new developments in the emergency health sector to humanitarian programming.
  • Advise on the coordination, implementation and prioritization of emergency health activities to ensure that efforts in assigned program areas are meeting the needs of affected populations and satisfy the goals and objectives of the response program.
  • As needed, provide technical support to State’s humanitarian nutrition and WASH Teams related to the complementary nature of these interventions to improve health outcomes in humanitarian settings.
  • As needed, serve on DARTs and serve on Washington-based Response Management Teams (RMTs), which provides services and support to DARTs deployed in response to disasters. The duties on RMTs will vary. (DARTs may require immediate (within 24 hours) deployment overseas for an extended period of time.)

Requirements

  • Post Graduate Studies (Master’s degree) plus seven (7) years of experience working in emergency relief and humanitarian assistance, and infectious disease outbreaks. A minimum of three (3) years of relevant experience must be obtained overseas.
  • Recent experience working in a technical capacity for an international nongovernmental organization, public international organization, or USG agency working in humanitarian relief and/or response in health and infectious disease outbreaks.
  • Fluency in critical concepts of emergency/ humanitarian health interventions in humanitarian contexts and ability to develop and guide programming to reflect those standards.
  • Understanding of key health issues related to displaced populations, refugees and other vulnerable populations and ability to represent the humanitarian perspective.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret strategy; to analyze, develop and present work results; and to monitor and evaluate implementation of programs.
  • Demonstrated flexibility and openness in responding to changing work priorities and environments.
  • Fluency in French and experience in the Democratic Republic of Congo strongly preferred.
  • US citizenship with an Active Secret Clearance required.

Working Conditions and Physical Requirements:

  • This position requires the ability to deploy for international travel assignments for at least one month at a time, as well as occasional domestic travel to Washington, DC.
  • When not travelling, this is a fully remote position within the United States and its territories.
  • Consultant may be requested for additional domestic or international travel up to 21 days.

Job Description

We're Concentrix. The global technology and services leader that powers the world’s best brands, today and into the future. We’re solution-focused, tech-powered, intelligence-fueled.   • Have excellent time management skills and the ability to work independently in a field-based environment
  • Have a valid driver’s license and required travel documents
  • Are able to travel up to 3 weeks per month, including Monday and Friday travel as business needs require
  • Ideally live near a major airport to support frequent business travel

It will be a plus if you:

  • Have B2B sales experience
  • Have experience selling specialized marketing services or experience in the marketing services industry
  • Have a proven track record of consistently exceeding sales goals
  • Have established experience building strategic business partnerships with automotive dealers or OEM field teams
  • Are located in Ontario or another location with convenient airport access

What's in it for you

We challenge conventions to deliver outcomes unimagined by creating customer experiences that go beyond WOW.

Description

WHO WE ARE

Come join the company reinventing data security, empowering businesses to realize the full potential of their data. As the leading data security platform purpose-built for the cloud era, Cyera’s mission is to reinvent how businesses secure data, enable agile collaboration, and boldly pursue new business opportunities. Trusted by security teams at leading global businesses, our team is proving that data security is the next big thing in cyber. Backed by the world’s leading investors and working with a large and growing list of Fortune 1000 companies, we are looking for world-class talent to join us as we usher in the new era of data security.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We’re hiring a Creative Director to bring Cyera’s brand to life across every campaign and every touchpoint where a customer, prospect, or employee meets us. Reporting to the Head of Corporate Marketing, you will be a key strategic leader of Cyera’s brand and a core creative voice on the marketing leadership team.

This is not an execution-only role. We’re looking for a creative leader who pairs strong visual instincts with strong writing, and who treats every campaign as a chance to tell a story people remember. You’ll partner closely with Design Studio, Integrated Marketing, and other functions across marketing to make sure Cyera’s brand shows up with the same craft and clarity everywhere it appears, and you’ll lead a small creative team that you’ll be expected to grow, in capability and in ambition.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Brand storytelling across campaigns. Turn Cyera’s positioning and messaging into campaigns that fuse strong visuals with strong copy. Define and build briefs that serve as a guide to make every campaign feel like one idea, carried consistently across every channel and format.
  • Creative direction for key touchpoints. Set the creative bar for the moments that matter most: launches, events, the website, sales collateral, social, and executive communications. Make sure the brand feels like one brand, wherever someone meets it.
  • Partnership with Design Studio. Work hand in hand with Design Studio to turn creative concepts into finished work. Bring clear direction, sharp feedback, and a point of view that raises the level of what gets made.
  • Partnership with Integrated Marketing. Sit alongside Integrated Marketing from the start of campaign planning, so creative is built into strategy rather than added at the end. Help turn campaign briefs into ideas that earn attention.
  • Creative team leadership. Lead, coach, and grow a small creative team across Copy and Video. Model the craft, help your team members develop into stronger creative thinkers, and build the bench for Cyera’s next stage of growth.
  • Brand stewardship. Act as a guardian of Cyera’s voice and identity across the company. Give partners across marketing, sales, and product the creative guardrails they need to move fast without losing consistency.

Requirements

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10-12 years of creative experience, including time as an art director, creative director, or similar role, ideally at a B2B technology company or a category-defining brand.
  • A portfolio that proves the partnership between visual and copy. You can point to campaigns where the idea, the design, and the words worked as one.
  • Enterprise brand experience. You know how to make a serious, technical brand feel human and memorable without losing credibility.
  • Hands-on craft. You can sketch a concept, sharpen a headline, or direct a shoot yourself, not just brief someone else to do it.
  • AI fluency. You know how to define where and how AI tools fit into the creative process, using them to raise quality and velocity together rather than trading one for the other.
  • Strong stakeholder management. You build trust with partners across marketing, sales, and product, and you know how to hold a creative point of view while navigating competing priorities.
  • People leadership. You’ve hired, coached, and grown creative talent, and people want to do their best work for you.
  • Collaborative range. You work well with design, marketing, and brand strategy partners, and you know how to hold a creative point of view without slowing a team down.
  • Operating principles that match ours, push boundaries, own and act, elevate together, and a leadership style that matches ours, model, coach, care.

COMPENSATION INFORMATION:

Compensation Range: $190,000-$230,000.

This compensation range represents Cyera’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation for this role at the time of posting, and Cyera may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. The final salary for this position will be determined in Cyera’s sole discretion, consistent with applicable law, and based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to the employee’s work experience, skills, and qualifications for the role, as well as the needs of Cyera’s business and other operational considerations.

Final compensation will vary based on seniority and relevance of experience, location, and position requirements.

This role may be eligible for potential merit increases based on factors such as individual or company performance, time in role, and other discretionary factors.

﻿BENEFITS - Why Cyera?

  • Ability to work remotely, with office setup reimbursement
  • Competitive salary
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Paid holidays and sick time
  • Health, vision, and dental insurance
  • Life, short and long-term disability insurance

Accounting GeneralDepartment

Vantage Accounting Operations is a shared services team responsible for accurately and efficiently recording financial transactions while building positive financial relationships with customers and vendors across North America.

The team coordinates the entry, review, and approval of day-to-day transaction processing in accordance with financial policies and departmentSLAs. The team members proactively engage in solving problems through close collaboration with internal and external stakeholders in the development and implementation of continuous process improvements by maximizing the use of our technology resources, and continuing education to improve accounting operational efficiency through assessing, standardizing, and streamlining day-to-day processes. POSITION SUMMARY:

The Senior Accountant plays a critical role within the Accounting Department and is responsible for the Month-End Financial close including: preparing monthly journal entries, performing balance sheet reconciliations, financial analyses, system controls, management reports, assisting with the annual budget and audit processes, and performing other accounting duties as assigned. This position reports to the Accounting Manager, though you will have the opportunity to work with different members of the Accounting, Finance, and Operations teams.

Position: Senior Accountant

Department: Accounting

Schedule: Full Time

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES / DUTIES:

JOB ROLES

  • Support the month and year-end close process by preparing expense accruals, preparing and reviewing journal entries and ensuring accuracy of financial statements.
  • Conduct monthly account reconciliations to ensure accurate reporting and ledger maintenance.
  • Coordinate and participate in internal and external audits, providing audit query documentation upon request.
  • Work closely with the Finance team to ensure proper general ledger coding of standard and non-standard transactions.
  • Conducts a monthly variance analysis to budget and identifies variance causes and trends.
  • Drive process improvement and automation to enhance efficiency and accuracy of accounting functions.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams on projects and support other business initiatives.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Minimum Qualifications:

EDUCATION:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance.
  • 5-7 years accounting experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • CPA.
  • Master's degree in Accounting or Finance.
  • Healthcare Accounting experience.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS:

  • Strong knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)
  • Must be able to work independently with minimal supervision, ability to multitask, and prioritize deadlines and schedules.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate complex accounting issues across all levels of the organization.
  • Proficiency in General Ledger systems and Microsoft O􀆯ice Suite (Word and Excel) with the ability to train others.
  • Must have strong analytical, problem solving, and organizations skills, with the ability to apply them in a non-profit healthcare environment.
  • Positive attitude and professional demeanor. Must be a dedicated team player with the willingness and ability to assist in other areas of the department as needed.

Compensation Range:

$62,500.00- $91,000.00

This range offers an estimate based on the minimum job qualifications. However, our approach to determining base pay is comprehensive, and a broad range of factors is considered when making an offer. This includes education, experience, skills, and certifications/licensures as they directly relate to position requirements; as well as business/organizational needs, internal equity, and market-competitiveness. In addition, BMCHS offers generous total compensation that includes, but is not limited to, benefits (medical, dental, vision, pharmacy), discretionary annual bonuses and merit increases, Flexible Spending Accounts, 403(b) savings matches, paid time off, career advancement opportunities, and resources to support employee and family well-being.

raw.excerpt: The Opportunity: The Process Safety Manager – Europe serves as the regional subject matter expert and leader for process safety, major accident prevention, and hazardous materials risk management across European operations.
raw.description:
The Opportunity:

The Process Safety Manager – Europe serves as the regional subject matter expert and leader for process safety, major accident prevention, and hazardous materials risk management across European operations. This position is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving process safety programs that protect employees, contractors, communities, company assets, and the environment while ensuring compliance with applicable European, local country, and company requirements.


The role provides technical leadership and governance for process safety management (PSM), risk assessment, management of change (MOC), major hazard prevention programs, fire and explosion prevention, hazardous materials management, emergency preparedness, and process safety performance improvement initiatives. The Process Safety Manager partners closely with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Quality, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, and site leadership teams to identify, assess, and mitigate process safety risks.


As a key member of the global EHS organization, the Process Safety Manager ensures alignment with corporate process safety standards while supporting country-specific regulatory obligations including Seveso III Directive requirements and other European major accident prevention regulations. The position requires approximately 35% travel to support audits, risk assessments, incident investigations, project reviews, emergency preparedness exercises, and facility engagement activities across Europe.

MAJOR JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES (List in order of importance)

Process Safety Leadership & Governance

  • Provide strategic leadership for process safety management programs across European operations.
  • Develop and implement regional process safety strategies aligned with corporate standards and business objectives.
  • Establish and maintain process safety governance systems, expectations, and performance metrics.
  • Promote a strong process safety culture through leadership engagement, employee involvement, and continuous improvement.

Regulatory Compliance & Major Accident Prevention

  • Ensure compliance with applicable European, national, and local process safety and hazardous materials regulations.
  • Provide technical expertise regarding Seveso III requirements and other major accident prevention regulations.
  • Support facility compliance programs related to hazardous substances, fire protection, explosion prevention, and emergency planning.
  • Interface with regulatory agencies and support inspections, audits, permitting activities, and regulatory submissions.

Process Hazard Analysis & Risk Management

  • Lead and facilitate Process Hazard Analyses (PHA) utilizing methodologies such as HAZOP, What-If, FMEA, Layer of Protection Analysis (LOPA), and other recognized risk assessment techniques.
  • Ensure timely completion and revalidation of hazard assessments.
  • Develop risk reduction recommendations and monitor implementation of corrective actions.
  • Evaluate process safety risks associated with existing and new operations.

Management of Change (MOC)

  • Lead and oversee Management of Change processes for equipment, technology, process, organizational, and procedural changes.
  • Evaluate proposed modifications for process safety risks and compliance impacts.
  • Ensure appropriate technical review, approval, and documentation of changes.
  • Verify implementation of risk mitigation actions before startup.

Engineering & Capital Project Support

  • Provide process safety oversight for capital projects, facility expansions, equipment upgrades, and new process introductions.
  • Participate in design reviews, hazard evaluations, pre-startup safety reviews, and commissioning activities.
  • Ensure process safety requirements are incorporated into project design and execution.
  • Support safe integration of new technologies and operational processes.

Incident Investigation & Organizational Learning

  • Lead investigations of significant process safety incidents, near misses, fires, explosions, chemical releases, and high-potential events.
  • Apply structured root cause analysis methodologies to identify systemic causes.
  • Develop corrective and preventive actions and monitor effectiveness.
  • Share lessons learned across sites to strengthen organizational learning and risk reduction.

Fire, Explosion & Hazardous Materials Risk Management

  • Oversee programs related to combustible dusts, flammable liquids, reactive chemicals, compressed gases, and hazardous materials storage.
  • Evaluate facility safeguards related to fire prevention, explosion protection, loss prevention, and emergency response.
  • Support process safety requirements related to chemical handling, storage, segregation, and transportation.

Audit, Assurance & Continuous Improvement

  • Develop and execute process safety audit programs for European facilities.
  • Conduct site assessments to verify compliance with corporate and regulatory requirements.
  • Track audit findings and facilitate closure of corrective actions.
  • Benchmark industry best practices and recommend opportunities for performance improvement.

Mechanical Integrity & Operational Excellence

  • Support development and oversight of mechanical integrity programs for critical process equipment.
  • Collaborate with Maintenance and Engineering teams to improve asset reliability and risk management.
  • Review inspection, testing, preventive maintenance, and integrity management practices.
  • Monitor performance indicators to identify emerging risks and opportunities.

Training & Workforce Development

  • Develop and deliver process safety training programs for employees, contractors, engineers, supervisors, and site leaders.
  • Coach facility teams on process safety principles, risk assessment methodologies, and regulatory requirements.
  • Serve as a technical resource for process safety-related questions and problem solving.

Emergency Preparedness & Business Continuity

  • Support emergency response planning and major incident preparedness activities.
  • Participate in emergency drills, exercises, and crisis management initiatives.
  • Evaluate emergency response capabilities related to hazardous material incidents and process upsets.
  • Assist facilities in strengthening resilience and business continuity planning.

QUALIFICATIONS (Education/Training, Experience and/or Certifications)

Education / Training

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Process Engineering, Occupational Safety, or a related technical discipline.

Preferred

  • Master's degree in Engineering, Process Safety, Risk Management, Safety Management, or a related field.

Experience

Required

  • Minimum 8–10 years of progressive experience in process safety, EHS, engineering, manufacturing, chemical processing, pharmaceuticals, specialty materials, energy, or industrial operations.
  • Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, and managing Process Safety Management programs.
  • Experience facilitating Process Hazard Analyses and risk assessments.
  • Experience leading incident investigations and Management of Change programs.
  • Proven success working with cross-functional operational and engineering teams across multiple locations.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting European manufacturing operations.
  • Experience with Seveso-regulated facilities or major accident hazard programs.
  • Experience supporting capital projects, facility expansions, and new process introductions.
  • Experience working within multinational organizations.

Certifications

Preferred

  • Certified Process Safety Professional (CCPSC)
  • Certified Safety Professional (CSP)
  • Chartered Engineer (CEng) or equivalent engineering registration
  • NEBOSH Diploma or equivalent professional safety qualification
  • Functional Safety or Risk Management certification
  • OSHA 30-Hour General Industry Certification
  • Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (Those necessary to perform the job competently)

  • Extensive knowledge of process safety principles, risk management systems, and major accident prevention programs.
  • Strong understanding of Seveso III Directive requirements and European process safety regulations.
  • Knowledge of OSHA PSM, EPA RMP, CCPS Risk-Based Process Safety principles, NFPA standards, and related industry frameworks.
  • Expertise in hazard identification and risk assessment methodologies including HAZOP, LOPA, FMEA, Bow-Tie Analysis, and What-If reviews.
  • Strong knowledge of Management of Change, Mechanical Integrity, Incident Investigation, and Emergency Response systems.
  • Ability to evaluate fire, explosion, chemical release, and process upset hazards.
  • Strong analytical, investigative, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to effectively influence leaders and stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities across geographically dispersed operations.
  • Skilled in technical report writing, performance metrics development, and audit management.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and EHS management systems.
  • Ability to interpret complex technical and regulatory requirements and translate them into practical operational solutions.
  • Strong business acumen and decision-making capability in high-risk operational environments.

ENVIRONMENTAL WORKING CONDITIONS & PHYSICAL EFFORT (Under Typical Positions)

  • Environmental Working Conditions & Physical Effort
  • Position is primarily remote/home-office based with regular travel to manufacturing, distribution, laboratory, warehouse, and processing facilities throughout Europe.
  • Approximately 35% travel is required, including domestic and international travel, overnight stays, and occasional short-notice site visits.
  • Exposure to manufacturing and industrial environments involving chemicals, hazardous materials, machinery, elevated work platforms, confined spaces, construction activities, and process equipment.
  • Must be able to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hard hats, hearing protection, safety footwear, and respiratory protection where required.
  • Frequent walking through industrial facilities, climbing stairs and ladders, and conducting field inspections.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds occasionally.
  • Ability to sit, stand, walk, bend, reach, and work on a computer for extended periods.
  • Must be capable of responding to emergency situations, participating in audits and investigations, and accessing operational areas as needed.
  • Ability to travel internationally and maintain flexibility to support business needs across multiple countries and time zones.

Job Description

Job Description:

The Senior Data Architect, Research Analytics will lead the South Carolina Clinical and Translational Science (SCTR) Institute’s data and reporting strategy and will engage with enterprise IS data leadership and teams to strategize for the design, creation, refinement, and long-term sustainability of an enterprise research data repository that integrates and curates' data from multiple disparate systems across the research lifecycle. This role serves as a critical technical and strategic partner to IS and research leadership and administration, finance, operations, compliance, and analytics teams.

The Senior Data Architect will lead the development of a trusted, scalable research data environment supporting SCTR’s metric tracking and reporting and continuous quality improvement data strategy and decision-making. The position will enable comprehensive reporting across financial performance, awards, earned revenue, operational efficiency, research performance, regulatory compliance, and study and participant-level metrics.


Job Duties:

Research Data Repository Architecture & Design 20%

  • Engage with enterprise IS Data teams to design and maintain the logical and physical architecture of a centralized research repository integrating data from numerous source systems, including but not limited to:
  • Financial systems (awards, expenditures, revenue, effort)
  • Grants and contracts management systems
  • Clinical trial management systems (CTMS)
  • Research service request systems (SPARC)
  • Institutional Review Board (IRB) and Compliance Systems
  • Learning management and training systems
  • Human resources and faculty appointment systems

Define standards for data modeling, normalization, dimensional modeling, and metadata management to ensure data quality, scalability, and performance


Data Integration & Curation 20%

  • Lead the development of robust ETL/ELT pipelines to ingest, harmonize, and curate data from disparate systems with varying structures, definitions, and data quality.
  • Ensure alignment between System APIs, and Integrations looking at workflows of systems such as RIMD, SPARC, CTMS, IRB, Epic, and financial systems.
  • Establish and document authoritative data sources, business rules, and transformation logic for research metrics.
  • Ensure consistent representation of investigators, departments, academic medical center (AMC) affiliations, colleges, and organizational hierarchies across systems.
  • Implement processes to manage historical data, changes to organizational structures, and longitudinal reporting. (Essential)

Research Metrics & Analytics Enablement 15%

  • Translate business requirements into data models and visualizations across key research domains, including:

o Financial performance (awards, expenditures, earned revenue, cost recovery)

o Research portfolio and award activity

o Operational performance and efficiency

o Research study activation timelines and cycle times

o Participant recruitment volumes, accrual rates, and demographic characteristics

o IRB approvals, protocol status, and regulatory timelines

o Required training and compliance approvals

  • Ensure the data mart supports reproducible, auditable research metrics used for internal and external reporting.

Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) 15%

  • Partner with research operations and quality teams to enable data-driven continuous quality improvement initiatives.
  • Develop metrics and dashboards that identify process bottlenecks, variability, and opportunities for improvement across the research lifecycle.
  • Support longitudinal trend analysis and benchmarking to assess the impact of operational changes.

Leadership Reporting & Workforce Planning 10%

  • Support SCTR and research leadership and grant reporting by delivering reliable, interpretable data for strategic decision-making.
  • Enable analyses used to justify workforce hires, capacity needs, and resource allocation based on research volume, complexity, and performance indicators.
  • Ensure visualizations and KPIs are suitable for board-level, sponsor-facing, and regulatory reporting.

Data Governance, Quality & Security 10%

  • Collaborate with data governance bodies to define data ownership, stewardship, access controls, and usage standards and support evaluation requests for integrating new vendor promoted tools and technologies into existing infrastructure.
  • Implement data quality monitoring, validation, and remediation processes.

Ensure compliance with institutional policies and applicable regulations related to data privacy, security, and research compliance.


Stakeholder Collaboration & Communication 10%

  • Act as a technical liaison between SCTR, IT, research administration, clinical research teams, finance, and institutional leadership.
  • Translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable insights for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to analysts, data engineers, and reporting teams.

MUSC Minimum Training and Experience Requirements:

A bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems or a related field and four years’ experience in systems development and maintenance, technical support or the support of complex database management systems. Related experience may be substituted for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis.

Additional Job Description

Minimum Requirements: A bachelor's degree and four years experience in automated information or communication system design, installation, operation, repair, sales or marketing. Related experience may be substituted for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis. Vaga 100% remota

Aqui a gente conecta o mundo

Sensedia é uma multinacional brasileira provedora de plataforma de gerenciamento de APIs, governança de agentes e soluções de integração, além de serviços profissionais. A companhia impulsiona a transformação digital de grandes empresas habilitando arquiteturas mais ágeis, modernas e escaláveis, possibilitando assim que seus clientes ofereçam produtos e experiências digitais a todo o seu ecossistema.

Trabalhar aqui é pertencer a uma cultura plural, descontraída e inovadora. É para quem tem coragem de ir além, pensar e agir fora da caixa. Preferimos pedir desculpas ao invés de pedir permissão e estamos sempre dispostos a nos transformar, nos reinventar.
Nossas pessoas são incríveis e você pode fazer parte disso tudo. Nos comprometemos em garantir um ambiente de trabalho acolhedor e respeitoso.

Conheça + em nosso site:


Qual a missão do Cargo?

Construir e evoluir soluções de software robustas, escaláveis e sustentáveis, atuando como referência técnica no desenvolvimento de APIs, aplicações e integrações. Contribuir para decisões técnicas e arquiteturais, garantindo qualidade, segurança e boas práticas de engenharia, além de apoiar o desenvolvimento do time e a evolução contínua das nossas soluções.

Quais serão suas atividades do dia-a-dia?

  • Projetar, desenvolver e evoluir APIs e serviços utilizando C# e .NET.
  • Desenvolver e orientar a construção de aplicações web com TypeScript e React.
  • Definir soluções para integrações síncronas, assíncronas e orientadas a eventos.
  • Projetar o uso de filas e tópicos considerando ordenação, idempotência, retentativas, dead-letter, concorrência e garantia de entrega.
  • Transformar requisitos funcionais em soluções técnicas sustentáveis.
  • Tomar e documentar decisões técnicas e arquiteturais.
  • Definir padrões de desenvolvimento, testes, observabilidade e segurança.
  • Diagnosticar problemas complexos de desempenho, integração e produção.
  • Apoiar pipelines de CI/CD, automação de infraestrutura e estratégias de implantação.
  • Realizar revisões de código e orientar profissionais menos experientes.
  • Atuar em conjunto com arquitetura, produto, UX, QA, segurança e operações.
  • Avaliar riscos, dependências e impactos antes da implementação.

Quais são os requisitos obrigatórios para esse cargo?

  • Experiência sólida com desenvolvimento backend utilizando C# e .NET, incluindo construção e evolução de APIs e serviços;
  • Experiência com desenvolvimento de aplicações web utilizando TypeScript e React;
  • Conhecimento sólido em arquiteturas de integração, incluindo comunicação síncrona, assíncrona e orientada a eventos;
  • Experiência com mensageria, filas e tópicos, considerando conceitos como ordenação, idempotência, retentativas, dead-letter, concorrência e garantia de entrega;
  • Capacidade de transformar requisitos funcionais e de negócio em soluções técnicas escaláveis, sustentáveis e de fácil evolução;
  • Experiência na tomada e documentação de decisões técnicas e arquiteturais;
  • Conhecimento de boas práticas e padrões relacionados a desenvolvimento, testes, observabilidade e segurança;
  • Experiência na investigação e resolução de problemas complexos de performance, integração e produção;
  • Conhecimento de CI/CD, automação de infraestrutura e estratégias de deployment;
  • Experiência com code review e capacidade de orientar tecnicamente profissionais menos experientes;
  • Capacidade de atuar de forma colaborativa com diferentes disciplinas, como Arquitetura, Produto, UX, QA, Segurança e Operações;
  • Capacidade de avaliar riscos técnicos, dependências e impactos para apoiar decisões antes da implementação.

Quais serão os requisitos diferencias para este cargo?

  • Experiência com Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) para execução e gerenciamento de aplicações conteinerizadas;
  • Conhecimento de serviços Azure voltados a integração, mensageria e comunicação em tempo real, como Event Grid, Event Hubs e SignalR;
  • Experiência com Infraestrutura como Código (IaC) utilizando Bicep ou Terraform;
  • Conhecimento e aplicação de práticas de DevSecOps, integrando segurança ao ciclo de desenvolvimento e entrega de software;
  • Experiência no desenho e evolução de soluções em cloud com foco em alta disponibilidade, escalabilidade, resiliência e otimização de custos;
  • Vivência em projetos de modernização de sistemas legados, incluindo evolução arquitetural, integração e adoção de tecnologias e práticas mais modernas.

Aqui você vai encontrar:

  • Vale Refeição/Vale Alimentação (Cartão Flash benefícios), Plano de Saúde, Plano Odontológico, Seguro de Vida, PPR, TotalPass, Auxílio Creche, Programa Well-Being (destinado para saúde física e mental), Universidade Corporativa (nossa #SensediaAcademy), com diversas trilhas de desenvolvimento; Parceiros culturais e educacionais, com descontos especiais; Somos uma empresa cidadã, proporcionando licença maternidade e licença paternidade estendida.

  • Temos #WorkWhereYouBelong como proposta de valor, que é um modelo flexível de trabalho que nos ajuda a aumentar o senso de pertencimento dos Sensediers.
    Trabalhe onde você pertence, porque as barreiras físicas estão menores, e o sentimento é de que exista apenas uma Sensedia em qualquer lugar que você esteja trabalhando.

Esta oportunidade também é para PCD! ;)

Suas experiências são compatíveis? Se candidate e venha conhecer a maior referência de APIs no Brasil! Queremos você em nossa equipe!!

  • Pensando em promover times cada vez mais diversos e ambientes de trabalho plurais, nossa missão é mapear os diferentes públicos que alcançamos com ele! Por isso, faremos algumas perguntinhas relacionadas à diversidade*, tudo bem? =)

raw.description:
Who we are:

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit to learn more.

About the Role:

As a GTM Engineer on the Deal Desk team, you’ll build and own practical AI-powered workflows, automations, and agents that improve how our Sales and GTM teams operate. You will be an operational Builder, continually scanning Deal Desk workflows for AI-solvable problems, turning team and stakeholder challenges into scalable, repeatable tools. You’ll partner with Deal Desk, Product, ESYS, and business stakeholders to identify high-value use cases, prototype solutions, launch secure production tools, and measure adoption and business impact for teams ranging from SMB to Strategic. You will own the full development lifecycle for internal Deal Desk AI tools, from initial prototyping and proof-of-concept development through production scaling, beta testing with end users, ongoing maintenance, and continuous improvement. The ideal candidate has practical business experience on a GTM or RevOps team.

We're looking for someone with an experimentation mindset—eager to prototype, learn quickly from failure, and explore new ideas. You should be passionate about AI’s potential to transform work and have a strong grasp of concepts like context windows, token usage, compute costs, chunking, and performance benchmarks. Experience with scripting, SQL/SOQL, Python basics, and prompt engineering using models like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, etc., via web and API is essential. Familiarity with the evolving agentic ecosystem, and the ability to explain technical topics to non-technical audiences, especially in a GTM context, is key.

What You'll Do:

  • Operate with the default question: “How can I use AI to solve this?”, consistently identifying Deal Desk bottlenecks to automate in order to provide the best possible experience for our stakeholders.
  • Design robust human-in-the-loop validation, audit trails, and fallback rules for Deal Desk agents to ensure complete compliance with revenue recognition policies and pricing approval matrices.
  • Own the full development cycle of prototyping / developing proof of concepts, scaling prototypes for production use, beta testing with end users, and performing ongoing maintenance for internal AI tools that support our GTM/Deal Desk and Sales partners. This includes building agents and workflows using Glean, Salesforce—including Agentforce and ClaudeForce—and n8n; developing front-end applications using Retool, Cursor, React, or similar tools; integrating enterprise data and APIs securely; and creating prompts and workflows for models such as Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity.
  • Ensure agents and applications follow UX best practices and can be easily leveraged by a less technical business audience
  • Manage a cost envelope for production use cases, testing different LLM models to balance performance with token consumption cost
  • Create and maintain documentation around launched solutions
  • Train end-users on the usage of launched tools

What We're Looking For:

  • 5-7 years of hands-on Deal Desk or RevOps experience, including solving business challenges with tooling, building and deploying internal tools, automations, data products, or AI-enabled workflows in an enterprise environment. Relevant backgrounds may include AI/ML engineering, Salesforce or business systems, data, software development, or workflow automation.
  • Hands-on experience with CPQ and CLM platforms
  • Strong understanding of AI fundamentals such as context windows, token consumption, compute cost, chunking, and performance benchmarks
  • Understanding of API usage, limitations, and how to leverage API’s to aggregate data across multiple source platforms. This includes an understanding of rate limits scalable API use as it pertains to both data sources and LLM’s
  • Understanding of scripting, SQL / SOQL, and Python fundamentals
  • Experience leveraging foundational models (Gemini, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Grok and others), both through the web interface and via the API
  • Familiarity with the rapidly evolving agentic landscape, including orchestration layers, MCP, Agent2Agent, and Salesforce-native agent platforms such as Agentforce and ClaudeForce. Experience building agents, workflows, or React-based user interfaces directly within Salesforce is preferred.

Pay Transparency
Your compensation may be based on several factors, including education, work experience, and certifications. For certain roles, total compensation may include restricted stock units. Motive offers benefits including health, pharmacy, optical and dental care benefits, paid time off, sick time off, short term and long term disability coverage, life insurance as well as 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). Learn more about our benefits by visitingMotive Perks & Benefits.

$140,000—$160,000 USD

The Cybersecurity Threat Detection & Automation Manager will lead a team responsible for designing, developing, automating, tuning, and continuously improving advanced threat detection and response capabilities across enterprise, cloud, identity, endpoint, email, network, SaaS, and manufacturing/OT environments.

This is a hands-on player/coach leadership role. The successful candidate will not only manage, mentor, and set direction for a team of detection engineering and automation professionals, but will also remain deeply involved in technical delivery. This includes reviewing detection logic, shaping automation workflows, validating use cases, improving alert fidelity, and ensuring the program produces measurable security outcomes.

The role is critical to reducing attacker dwell time, improving investigation quality, scaling response through automation, and strengthening the organization’s overall SecOps maturity through SIEM, SOAR, detection lifecycle governance, and engineering discipline.

The ideal candidate combines deep detection engineering expertise, automation experience, incident response knowledge, strong leadership ability, and the program management discipline needed to build scalable cybersecurity capabilities in a complex enterprise environment.

The Impact You Will Make

In this role, you will help modernize and mature the organization’s threat detection and response capabilities. You will lead the team responsible for turning adversary behavior, threat intelligence, incident lessons learned, red team findings, and business risk into actionable detections, automation workflows, analyst guidance, and measurable security outcomes.

  • Detection coverage across enterprise, cloud, identity, endpoint, email, network, OT, and SaaS environments
  • Alert fidelity and false-positive reduction
  • Investigation speed and analyst consistency
  • SOAR automation maturity and response scalability
  • Detection lifecycle governance, testing, validation, and documentation
  • SecOps modernization across SIEM, SOAR, EDR, threat intelligence, and telemetry platforms
  • Reduced manual triage and improved operational repeatability

Industry: Business AI Platform Subscriptions
Location: Remote
Employment Type: Full-time
Working Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM AEST
Primary Tools: GoHighLevel (GHL) CRM, Zoom

Role Overview

We are seeking a commercially sharp, high-performing Business Development Manager to drive pipeline generation and close deals live on Zoom for our AI subscription platform.

This position owns the end-to-end sales lifecycle directly within GoHighLevel (GHL)—covering prospecting, multi-channel outbound outreach, inbound lead follow-up, demo booking, discovery, live product demonstrations, objection handling, and one-call closes (no formal proposals sent). You will sell directly to small to medium business (SMB) owners, solopreneurs, coaches, and service-based business leaders. Additionally, you will coordinate seamless post-sale handovers to guarantee rapid onboarding and exceptional customer satisfaction.

What You Will Sell (AUD)

  • Business AI Platform Annual Subscriptions (Includes AI Yourself)

Core Responsibilities

  • Pipeline Generation (Outbound & Inbound): Build targeted prospect lists aligned with our Ideal Customer Profile (ICP). Execute multi-channel outreach via GHL (email, SMS, calls, social touchpoints). Respond to inbound inquiries instantly with rigorous follow-up cadences.
  • Qualification & Discovery: Qualify leads based on fit, urgency, financial capacity, and decision-maker authority. Conduct structured discovery calls to unpack business pain points and desired outcomes; quickly disconfirm non-fits to preserve focus.
  • Live Demos & One-Call Closing: Execute high-impact Zoom demos communicating clear ROI, outcomes, and immediate action steps. Address objections confidently and close deals live using approved pricing and offer frameworks. Collect onboarding and payment details on the spot.
  • CRM Hygiene & Pipeline Forecasting: Maintain flawless GHL records (lead sources, activity logs, deal stages, and task schedules). Track daily/weekly operational metrics and deliver reliable pipeline forecasts using GHL analytics.
  • Handover & Customer Experience: Deliver clean, immediate handovers to customer success to accelerate onboarding. Identify strategic add-on, upsell, and referral opportunities during the transition.
  • Continuous Improvement: Refine scripts, messaging sequences, and audience targeting based on live call data. Share win/loss feedback to help optimize product positioning and onboarding workflows.

Requirements

  • Experience: 3+ years of success in B2B or B2C high-ticket sales, consultative sales, or business development.
  • Full-Funnel Capability: Proven ability to independently prospect, run discovery, and close (not just appointment setting).
  • Communication: Exceptional verbal, Zoom presence, and written English skills; highly comfortable guiding business owners to decisive buying actions.
  • Tech Stack: Proficiency with sales workflows and CRMs; direct experience with GoHighLevel (GHL) is strongly preferred.
  • Execution & Integrity: Highly structured with tasks, calendar management, and call notes. Operates with strict ethical standards (zero high-pressure tactics or exaggerated claims).

Compliance & Guardrails

  • Pricing Governance: Pricing and offer structures are fixed. Unauthorized discounting or custom deals are strictly prohibited.
  • Policy Compliance: Adhere strictly to company guidelines regarding data privacy, confidential information handling, compliant outreach practices, opt-out management, and accurate product representation.
  • Refund Policy: Customers receive comprehensive onboarding and support. Refunds are not provided for change of mind and are reviewed strictly on an exceptional basis at management discretion.

Benefits

  • Remote / WFH
  • Dayshift - AU Business Hours
  • Full time

Commercial Operations Coordinator

Location:Remote | Pacific Time Zone preferredEmployment Type: Full-Time

About the Role

We're looking for a highly organized, detail-oriented Business Operations Coordinator to support the backbone of our commercial and client operations. This is a cross-functional role sitting at the intersection of contract management, grant development, customer success, and business development — ideal for someone who thrives on variety, takes ownership, and wants to grow with a mission-driven clean transportation company.

You'll play a key supporting role managing public agency contracts and procurement relationships, help develop winning proposals and grant applications, and ensure our customers receive responsive, high-quality service.

What You'll Do

Contract Administration

  • Support day-to-day administration of contracts with large public agencies — including transit authorities, municipalities, and school districts — tracking deliverables, deadlines, and compliance requirements
  • Maintain organized contract documentation, amendments, and correspondence
  • Coordinate internally across teams to ensure contractual obligations are met on time
  • Assist with invoicing, reporting, and contract renewals as needed
  • Support onboarding of new clients and ensure smooth service delivery of contract requirements
  • Serve as a responsive point of contact for contract inquiries and requests

Grant Writing & RFP Support

  • Research funding opportunities, RFPs, and RFIs relevant to Camber's services and markets
  • Support the development of proposals, grant applications, and qualifications packages
  • Maintain a library of reusable proposal content, bios, past performance summaries, and compliance documents
  • Coordinate submission logistics to ensure on-time, complete responses

Marketing & Business Development Support

  • Help update website content, collateral, and presentations as needed
  • Support outreach efforts including research on prospective clients and HubSpot CRM data entry and maintenance
  • Assist with preparing materials for sales conversations, and follow-up communications

Why Join Camber

  • Be part of a team accelerating the transition to zero-emission fleets across North America
  • High-visibility, cross-functional role with real room to grow
  • Work remotely with a collaborative, mission-driven team

Requirements

What We're Looking For

Required
  • 2–5 years of experience in a sales, operations, administrative, or coordination role
  • Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail — you don't let things fall through the cracks
  • Strong written communication skills; comfortable drafting professional documents and correspondence
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; comfort learning new tools quickly

Nice to Have

  • Experience with government contracts, public agencies, or public procurement processes
  • Familiarity with grant writing or RFP response processes
  • Experience with HubSpot or similar CRM platforms
  • Interest in EVs, fleet electrification, clean energy, or infrastructure
No agencies or recruiters, please. We are not accepting unsolicited resumes or outreach from recruitment agencies or staffing firms. Any unsolicited submissions will not be considered and will not create any obligation on the part of Camber Charging.

U.S. employees are eligible for paid time away as described below, subject to Cisco’s policies:

  • Provide Institutional Sales and Affiliates with comprehensive call notes and market feedback—both positive and negative—on affiliate products and industry trends.

Position Summary

Casambi is seeking a motivated, strategic Regional Sales Director to lead growth across the Eastern half of North America. This senior sales leader will serve as the primary point of contact for the region, strengthening relationships with sales agents, specifiers, distributors, contractors, and other market partners while developing opportunities in underserved areas. Working closely with the Executive Vice President of Sales and cross-functional colleagues, the Regional Sales Director will translate company strategy into regional sales plans, build market coverage, improve pipeline visibility, and help customers understand the value of Casambi’s scalable lighting-control ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute a regional sales strategy aligned with company revenue, growth, and market-development objectives.
  • Establish annual and quarterly sales plans with agency partners, define measurable goals, and maintain regular communication on progress, opportunities, and risks.
  • Review agency dashboards, CRM data, pipeline activity, forecasts, and key performance indicators to drive accountability and informed decision-making.
  • Maintain and expand relationships with existing agents, specifiers, electrical engineers, architects, distributors, contractors, national accounts, and other industry partners.
  • Identify coverage gaps and recruit, interview, onboard, and develop new agents in unrepresented or underperforming markets.
  • Support agents and customers through joint sales calls, design discussions, presentations, product demonstrations, project meetings, and on-site visits.
  • Deliver continuing education, product training, and market-facing presentations that build partner confidence and position Casambi as a trusted controls resource.
  • Proactively identify and advance project opportunities from specification through order, coordinating internal resources to resolve commercial and technical barriers.
  • Monitor competitor activity, local market conditions, customer feedback, and industry trends; communicate actionable insights to sales, marketing, product, and support teams.
  • Represent Casambi at regional and national trade shows, industry events, partner meetings, and professional associations.
  • Maintain accurate and timely records of accounts, contacts, projects, activities, forecasts, and next steps in HubSpot and other company systems.
  • Manage regional resources responsibly, including travel planning, expense control, and prioritization of high-impact opportunities.
  • As the region grows, recruit, lead, coach, and develop two to three Regional Sales Managers, setting clear expectations and supporting strong performance.
  • Conduct company business through approved company devices, systems, and software, including Outlook, HubSpot, and Microsoft 365 applications.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, sales, marketing, engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • At least seven years of progressive experience in lighting, lighting controls, electrical supply, electrical design, or a closely related industry.
  • Proven outside-sales success across the agency, specification, distribution, contractor, or OEM channels.
  • Demonstrated ability to build territory plans, manage a sales pipeline, forecast accurately, and use performance data to improve results.
  • Strong relationship-building, negotiation, written communication, presentation, and public-speaking skills.
  • Highly organized, self-motivated, and comfortable working independently in a remote, fast-paced environment.
  • Sound judgment, executive presence, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while collaborating effectively across functions.
  • Proficiency with CRM platforms and Microsoft 365 applications; HubSpot experience is preferred.
  • Valid driver’s license and passport with the ability to travel frequently throughout the territory and periodically to national meetings and events.

Preferred Industry Knowledge

  • Established relationships with lighting agents, electrical engineers, architects, designers, distributors, contractors, or related partners in Eastern North America.
  • Working knowledge of the lighting-industry go-to-market model, project lifecycle, channel structure, and competitive landscape.
  • Ability to read construction drawings, lighting plans, specifications, and related project documents; experience with Bluebeam or similar software is preferred.
  • Knowledge of lighting-control protocols, ecosystems, system design, commissioning, and connected-building technologies is strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting wireless, wired, or hybrid lighting-control solutions is a plus.

Success in This Role

Success will be measured through sustainable regional revenue growth, healthy pipeline development, forecast accuracy, partner engagement, expanded market coverage, effective project conversion, CRM use, and strong cross-functional collaboration.

Compensation and Benefits

Casambi offers a competitive base salary and incentive program, along with medical, dental, and vision insurance options and other company-sponsored benefits. Specific compensation and benefits may vary based on experience, qualifications, and applicable requirements.

Equal Opportunity

Casambi is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace. Employment decisions are made based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to any status protected by applicable law. Reasonable accommodations are available for qualified individuals with disabilities during the application and employment process.

Trading Specialist

Reports to: Director, Trading
Employment Type: Full-Time
FLSA Status: Exempt, Salaried
Location: Remote (U.S.)

About Mutual

Mutual Group is a mission-driven, independent financial services firm founded more than 40 years ago and headquartered in Southern California. Through our broker-dealer and registered investment adviser subsidiaries, we support more than 1,600 financial professionals nationwide and oversee in excess of $13 billion in assets. Our culture is grounded in our values: Personal, Authentic, Collaborative, and Knowledgeable. We take pride in serving our advisors and clients with integrity, expertise, and care.

Position Overview

The Trading Specialist plays a key role in supporting the daily trading operations of Mutual Group’s advisory and brokerage accounts. This position is responsible for executing trades across a range of financial instruments, including equities, fixed income, ETFs, mutual funds, and options, in accordance with advisor models and instructions. The ideal candidate is accurate, efficient under pressure, and eager to grow their skills in a fast-paced environment.

This is an excellent opportunity for a self-starter looking to grow within a dynamic team while deepening their trading expertise and directly supporting the success of our advisor clients.

Responsibilities

Trade Execution and Rebalancing

  • Execute, manage, and monitor trades during market hours across multiple custodians and platforms.

  • Trade and rebalance portfolios across multiple asset classes (equities, fixed income, ETFs, mutual funds, options, and UITs) in accordance with advisor models and instructions.

  • Use third-party trading systems to calculate rebalances, allocate assets, and execute trades.

  • Review trading reports to identify accounts requiring action and ensure portfolios remain aligned with assigned models.

Advisor Support and Process Improvement

  • Research and troubleshoot trade-related issues in coordination with custodians and internal teams.

  • Support onboarding of new advisors, accounts, and portfolio models, ensuring trading integration is seamless.

  • Assist with trading-related activities such as cash management, distributions, and tax-loss harvesting.

  • Contribute to the development and refinement of trading procedures and documentation.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • Relevant experience in trading, operations, or investment support; three (3) or more years preferred.

  • Series 7 license.

  • Series 65 license, or willingness to obtain it within six months of hire.

  • Strong working knowledge of investment products and operational processes.

  • High level of accuracy and attention to detail, with the ability to work efficiently under pressure during market hours.

  • Strong communication skills, both written and oral.

  • Demonstrated problem-solving and decision-making skills.

Preferred

  • Familiarity with the Orion Eclipse trading platform.

  • Experience with custodians such as Fidelity, Schwab, and NFS.

  • Understanding of advisory account structures, 401(k) and 529 rebalancing, and annuity platforms.

Cultural Fit

The ideal candidate brings energy, accountability, and a service-oriented mindset to everything they do. They thrive in an environment that values collaboration over silos, candor over politics, and follow-through over flash. Specifically, the Trading Specialist embodies our values:

  • Personal: Builds genuine relationships with colleagues and advisors and treats every interaction as an opportunity to add value.

  • Authentic: Communicates honestly, owns mistakes, and is comfortable raising issues before they become problems.

  • Collaborative: Brings others along, shares credit generously, and works across functions without ego.

  • Knowledgeable: Demonstrates curiosity, asks thoughtful questions, and invests in learning the business they support.

Why Mutual

Joining Mutual means joining a financial services firm where the work you do has visible, tangible impact. We are big enough to support an established platform and small enough that individual contributions are seen, valued, and rewarded. We invest in our people through competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, ongoing professional development, and a leadership team that takes its responsibility to our employees as seriously as its responsibility to our advisors and clients.

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

  • 401(k) participation with company match

  • Paid time off and paid holidays

  • Eligibility for discretionary performance-based bonus

  • Wellness initiatives

  • Opportunities for continuous learning and professional development in a supportive team.

Salary Range

Annual base salary range (full-time equivalent):$75,000 to $95,000.

Final offer will be commensurate with the selected candidate’s experience and demonstrated capabilities. The position is also eligible for discretionary performance-based bonus consideration.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit a current resume and a brief cover letter describing their interest in the role and relevant trading, operations, or investment support experience to the firm at mutual.group/careers-join-our-team. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

Mutual Group is an equal opportunity employer. Candidates who need an accommodation during the application process may contact .

Salary: 75K - 95K USD a year

raw.description:
The Functional Architect – Workday Student (Australian Higher Education) is the functional leader for student administration engagements across Australian and New Zealand universities. This role is suited to an experienced higher education practitioner with hands-on experience across multiple student administration domains, such as student records, admissions, curriculum and academic structure, advising, student finance and compliance. Technical or systems experience is beneficial but not essential.

What matters most is a genuine interest in understanding how Workday works and the ability to connect platform capability with the realities of university operations. The person who fits this role will be energised by the opportunity to help shape how Workday is applied across the higher education sector.

They serve as the functional leader on Workday Student implementations and are accountable for bringing together the full student lifecycle as it exists in Workday and as it operates within an Australian or New Zealand university. This includes admissions, enrolment, progression, assessment, student finance, graduation and regulatory reporting.

The incumbent is trusted to form a point of view, guide solution direction and make well-informed decisions drawing on their sector knowledge and practitioner experience. Working closely with Engagement Managers, functional leads and senior university stakeholders, they help deliver solutions that are practical, compliant, sustainable and aligned to institutional objectives.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead the functional architecture for Workday Student programs from discovery through deployment and stabilisation.
  • Own the end-to-end student lifecycle design, ensuring admissions, student records, curriculum and academic structure, advising, progression, assessment, student financials and graduation operate as one connected solution.
  • Ensure localised solutions are fit for purpose, operationally sustainable and compliant with Australian and New Zealand regulatory obligations, including TCSI, HELP/eCAF, TEQSA, ESOS/CRICOS, PRISMS, admissions pathways, census and EFTSL requirements.
  • Maintain a current understanding of Workday capabilities, releases, AI and agent innovations, translating emerging functionality into practical guidance and roadmap recommendations for universities.
  • Translate institutional strategy, academic policy and regulatory requirements into clear solution principles, design decisions and implementation roadmaps.
  • Facilitate cross-functional design forums and guide stakeholders through complex decisions, dependencies and trade-offs across the student lifecycle.
  • Provide oversight of business processes, security, integrations, reporting, data conversion, testing and deployment readiness to ensure a cohesive solution.
  • Review key design artefacts, configuration outcomes, risks, assumptions and decisions for completeness, quality and alignment to client objectives.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to university leaders, helping shape sustainable operating models and future capability roadmaps.
  • Mentor consultants and functional leads, promoting consistent methods, reusable assets and continuous improvement across the practice.
  • Support pursuits through solution shaping, estimation, demonstrations, proposal development and client presentations.

Duties & Tasks:

  • Lead and facilitate client workshops, design forums and decision-making sessions across multiple student administration domains.
  • Work closely with Engagement Managers, functional leads and technical teams to identify and manage cross-functional dependencies, risks and design impacts.
  • Review solution designs, configuration outcomes and key project deliverables to ensure quality, consistency and alignment to client objectives.
  • Provide practical guidance to clients on regulatory, operational and organisational considerations that influence solution design.
  • Support delivery teams in resolving design blockers and navigating complex functional decisions.
  • Mentor consultants and functional leads, sharing sector knowledge, implementation experience and leading practices.
  • Participate in pursuit activities, including solution shaping, estimation, demonstrations and client presentations.
  • Maintain awareness of emerging trends in higher education administration and bring relevant insights into client conversations and solution design.
  • Stay current with Workday Student capabilities, releases, AI and agent innovations, and assess their relevance to Australian and New Zealand universities.
  • Identify gaps in our student administration IP and collaborate with practice director to close them – new design patterns, localisation assets, accelerators and methodology updates.
  • Support the sales team by:
    • Assisting Solution Architects with estimating projects, as necessary.
    • Participating in Sales Orals meetings for proposed assignments.
    • Assisting with or reviewing estimates for Change Orders in functional areas.
    • Participating in discussions regarding functional areas and localisation scope that may come into scope for a project or client.

Education and Experience Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent.
  • Current Workday Student certification, or the demonstrated capability and commitment to achieve certification.
  • Significant experience working within an Australian or New Zealand university in a student administration, academic services or related operational leadership role.
  • Demonstrated understanding of the end-to-end student lifecycle and the ability to translate higher education business requirements into practical solution outcomes.
  • Working knowledge of the Australian and New Zealand higher education regulatory environment, including obligations such as TCSI, HELP/eCAF, TEQSA, ESOS/CRICOS, PRISMS, admissions pathways, census and EFTSL reporting.
  • Experience leading design and decision-making across multiple student administration domains, such as admissions, student records, curriculum and academic structure, advising, progression, student finance and graduation.
  • Experience with Workday Student or a comparable student information system, including leading complex functional design discussions and resolving cross-functional dependencies.
  • Proven ability to facilitate workshops and communicate effectively with executives, academic leaders, professional staff and technical teams.
  • Experience supporting implementation activities including governance, testing, data conversion, integrations and deployment readiness.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide leadership in ambiguous situations, influence stakeholders and make sound decisions based on business and operational considerations.
  • Curiosity about emerging technology and a willingness to stay current with evolving Workday capabilities, including AI and agent innovations.

Why choose Cognizant:

  • Entrepreneurial environment that welcomes your ideas
  • Opportunity to do great work
  • Outreach programs that support communities and tap into your volunteer spirit
  • Learning opportunities to help current needs and advancement
  • Global operations, with opportunities in North America, Europe and Asia Pacific
  • An abundance of Affinity groups to meet your needs

Cognizant Core Values:

  • Work as One: We think beyond roles, relying on each other’s strengths to win as a team.
  • Raise the Bar: We always aim for excellence in how we work and what we deliver.
  • Dare to Innovate: We push boundaries and take chances to reimagine what’s possible.
  • Do the Right Thing: We all lead with integrity and always make the ethical choice.
  • Own It: We own the outcomes for our company, colleagues, and community.
